description: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India. The demographic data from the 2011 Census remains static until the next official census is published and is highly crucial for all UP state-level competitive exams.

sections.title: Total Population Overview
sections.description: Key statistics regarding the total population of Uttar Pradesh and its share at the national level.

important_facts.fact: The total population of Uttar Pradesh is approximately 19.98 Crore, which accounts for 16.51% of India's total population.
The male population constitutes 52.29%, while the female population accounts for 47.71% of the state's total population.
A vast majority of the state's population lives in rural areas (77.73%), while the urban population stands at 22.27%.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the most populous district (highest total population) in the state.
It is the least populous district (lowest total population) in the state.

sections.title: Literacy Rate
sections.description: Data highlighting the educational standards, including the overall, male, and female literacy rates across districts.

important_facts.fact: The overall literacy rate of Uttar Pradesh is 67.68%.
The male literacy rate in the state is 77.28%, while the female literacy rate is 57.18%.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: This district has the highest overall literacy rate (80.1%) and the highest male literacy rate in the state.
It has the lowest overall literacy rate, as well as the lowest male and lowest female literacy rates.
This district records the highest female literacy rate (75.1%) in Uttar Pradesh.

sections.title: Sex Ratio and Child Sex Ratio
sections.description: The sex ratio represents the number of females per 1,000 males, a critical indicator of demographic balance.

important_facts.fact: The overall Sex Ratio of Uttar Pradesh is 912 females per 1000 males (lower than the national average of 943).
The Child Sex Ratio (for the age group of 0 to 6 years) in Uttar Pradesh is 902.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It boasts the highest sex ratio in the state (1024), followed closely by Azamgarh (1019).
It records the lowest sex ratio (851) among all districts in the state.
This district has the highest Child Sex Ratio (950) in the state.

sections.title: Population Density and Decadal Growth
sections.description: Statistics regarding the number of people living per square kilometer and the population growth rate over 10 years.

important_facts.fact: The Population Density of Uttar Pradesh is 829 persons per square kilometer.
The Decadal Population Growth Rate of the state for the period 2001-2011 was recorded at 20.22%.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the most densely populated district with a population density of 3,971 persons per sq km.
It is the least densely populated district with a population density of only 242 persons per sq km.
This district experienced the highest decadal growth rate (49.1%).
This district recorded the lowest decadal growth rate (9.9%).

sections.title: Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)
sections.description: Crucial demographic distribution data concerning the SC and ST populations within the state.

important_facts.fact: The Scheduled Castes (SC) make up 20.69% of the state's total population. Uttar Pradesh has the highest total SC population in India.
The Scheduled Tribes (ST) constitute a very small fraction, making up just 0.57% of the state's total population.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Sitapur has the highest SC population in terms of absolute numbers, whereas Kaushambi has the highest SC population by percentage.
It is the district with both the highest ST population in absolute numbers and the highest ST percentage.
It records both the lowest SC population and the lowest ST population in the state.
